beats.narration_text: Someone asked if practicing IRAC with Claude means Claude hands you the finished answer. It doesn't — it walks you through the steps. So: does practicing IRAC with Claude give you the steps?

beats.narration_text: A Skill is a folder Claude reads before it acts. This one is called irac-practice. Its one file, SKILL.md, holds the whole instruction set for drilling IRAC — written in plain language, no hidden logic. Claude reads it, then acts. The file is the program.

The drill lives in a Steps section. Claude reads each step in order: pose the hypo, then wait for your Issue, your Rule, your Application, in that order. Linear — no skipping ahead, unless a step says otherwise.

production_viz.label: POSE, PAUSE, CHECK
production_viz.caption: linear — no skipping ahead unless a step says so

beats.narration_text: One check inside it is specific: stating the right Conclusion without showing the Application earns nothing — the Application is where the Rule actually meets the facts, one fact at a time. A Conclusion that skips it is a guess wearing the right answer.

production_viz.label: CONCLUSION, OR APPLICATION
production_viz.caption: only the Application actually earns credit

beats.narration_text: Claude isn't grading your Conclusion — it's checking whether you showed the Application, one fact at a time, on the way to it.

beats.narration_text: Your turn. Paste this into Claude: give me a short fact pattern, one paragraph. Read the irac-practice skill, and don't give me the answer — ask me for my Issue first, then my Rule, then my Application, and only check my Conclusion after I've given all three.
